correctness.rationale: A layered permutation has exactly one independent fair cut bit at each of its first n-1 gaps; the value order is definable from cuts. FO translates to an aperiodic DFA over 0/1 words with final 0, and every recurrent class of its rational transition matrix has a 0-fixed state, making the limit rational. For any b, explicit equal-length w_j=0^(t+3)1u_j1 are pairwise cross-bifix-free, so exchanging all occurrences of any two words is a bijection preserving occurrence starts. The finite-size probability of first label in any a-set is exactly a/b times probability of any occurrence, and one fixed word occurs with probability tending to one exponentially. First-occurrence tests are FO-definable in two orders. The checker tests bounded instances only; the infinite statement is proved symbolically.

originality.rationale: The new statement is the *entire* first-order limit probability set Q∩[0,1] for uniform layered permutations Av(231,312), including a uniform exact finite-size a/b symmetry and exponential convergence. Braunfeld–Kukla 2022 establishes convergence and implicitly rationality; Falgas-Ravry et al. 2026 Thm. 1.4 establishes density, not all-rational attainment. Berthé et al. 2025 concerns aperiodic language densities and their formulae, not the specific TOTO-spectrum equivalence. A narrower Fibonacci-class rational-attainment result does not imply this full-class spectrum; shared first-hit coding is acknowledged. Priority uncertainty remains concerning earlier coding/convex-order literature.
residual_risks: Older constructions via fair-coin patterns, self-synchronizing codes, prefix codes or aperiodic-language density may contain the all-rational realization as folklore or a stronger theorem.

The earlier rational-attainment finding for the Fibonacci subclass uses a related first-occurrence approach; the new result is distinguished by the full layered class and complete rational-only spectrum.

value.rationale: An exact complete limit spectrum is a naturally motivated invariant of a well-studied homogeneous permutation class, stronger than convergence and the currently established general dense-spectrum theorem. It identifies the sharp exclusion (all irrational values) and gives explicit first-order realizations with exponentially small error for every rational denominator. The full-class classification is not logically supplied by a prior attainment result for a stricter Fibonacci subclass. Quantifier optimality is not asserted.
